title: Person-by-Person 31 Dynasties of Egypt (Manetho, Palermo Stone, Willockx, Budge) + Complete Ptolemies & Kushite Kings

nodes.name: Manetho's Divine & Shemsu-Hor Horizon (Pre-Menes Era)
nodes.era: Predynastic Mythic Era (Manetho Fr. 1-4, Loeb pp. 3-19)
nodes.notes: Manetho's opening divine & demigod kingship sequence preceding Menes: Ptah -> Re -> Shu -> Geb -> Osiris -> Seth -> Horus -> 9 Demigods -> Shemsu-Hor ('Spirits of the Dead').

nodes.name: King Scorpion I/II & Palermo Stone Lower Egypt Kings (Dynasty 0)
nodes.role: Earliest Historically Inscribed Rulers of the Nile Before Narmer
nodes.notes: Pre-Unification Red Crown kings preserved on Row 1 of the Palermo Stone (Seka, Khayu, Tiu, Thesh, Neheb, Wazner, Mekh) alongside Upper Egyptian Dynasty 0 rulers Iry-Hor, Ka & King Scorpion.

nodes.name: Dynasty I Horizon (Thinite, 8 Kings, c. 2982–2803 BCE)
sources: Budge Book of Kings Vol. II
nodes.notes: 179 historical years (Manetho: 253 yrs); Africanus makes every king son of his predecessor.

nodes.name: Dynasty II Horizon (9 Kings, c. 2803–2657 BCE)
sources: Budge Book of Kings Vol. II
nodes.notes: Under Nynetjer (Binothris) it was decreed women could hold royal dignity.

nodes.name: Dynasty III Horizon (Memphite Step Pyramid Era, c. 2657–2589 BCE)
sources: Budge Book of Kings Vol. II
nodes.notes: Djoser & Imhotep built the Saqqara Step Pyramid; Huni inaugurated the royal cartouche.

nodes.name: Dynasty IV Horizon (Giza Great Pyramid Builders, c. 2589–2454 BCE)
sources: Budge Book of Kings Vol. II
nodes.notes: Sneferu, Khufu, Djedefre, Khafre, Baka, Menkaure, Shepseskaf & Queen Khentkawes.

nodes.name: Dynasty V Horizon (Solar Kings & Pyramid Texts, c. 2454–2297 BCE)
sources: Budge Book of Kings Vol. II
nodes.notes: Palermo Stone Annals compiled under Userkaf; oldest Pyramid Texts inscribed under Unas.

nodes.name: Dynasty VI Horizon (Memphite Old Kingdom Finale, c. 2297–2168 BCE)
nodes.role: Era of Pepi II & Queen Nitocris
sources: Budge Book of Kings Vol. II
nodes.notes: Concludes the Old Kingdom with 94-year reign of Pepi II and Queen Nitocris.

nodes.name: First Intermediate Period (Dynasties VII–X, Khety/Achthoes & Merikare)
nodes.era: c. 2168-2040 BCE (Manetho Fr. 23-30; Breasted Vol. I)
sources: Budge Book of Kings Vol. II
nodes.notes: Khety / Achthoes of Heracleopolis (Teaching for King Merikare).

nodes.name: Dynasty XI Horizon (Theban Middle Kingdom Unifiers, c. 2160–2000 BCE)
nodes.era: c. 2160-2000 BCE (Breasted Vol. I §63; Manetho Fr. 31-32)
sources: Budge Book of Kings Vol. II
nodes.notes: Intef I–III and Mentuhotep II–IV reunified Upper & Lower Egypt.

nodes.name: Dynasty XII Horizon (Middle Kingdom Golden Age, 2000–1788 BCE)
nodes.role: Classical Peak of Egyptian Literature & Labyrinth
sources: Budge Book of Kings Vol. II
nodes.notes: Manetho preserves direct parent-child succession through Queen Sobekneferu (Scemiophris).

nodes.name: Dynasties XIII–XIV Horizon (Second Intermediate Period)
sources: Budge Book of Kings Vol. II
nodes.notes: Sobekhotep IV (Chenephres in Artapanus) and Dedumose (Tutimaeus).

nodes.name: Dynasties XV–XVII Horizon (Great Hyksos & Theban Liberation)
nodes.era: c. 1650-1550 BCE (Manetho Fr. 42-49 via Josephus Against Apion)
nodes.role: Hyksos Rulers of Avaris & Theban Liberators
sources: Budge Book of Kings Vol. II
nodes.notes: Josephus (quoting Manetho verbatim) preserved the 6 Great Hyksos rulers until Seqenenre & Kamose launched liberation.

nodes.name: Dynasty XVIII Horizon (Thutmoside Empire, 1550–1391 BCE)
sources: Budge Book of Kings Vol. II
nodes.notes: Ahmose I through Hatshepsut, Thutmose III & Thutmose IV.

nodes.name: Dynasty XVIII Late Horizon (Amarna & Harmais/Danaus Transition)
sources: Budge Book of Kings Vol. II
nodes.notes: Manetho Fr. 50/53 identifies Horemheb ('Harmais') = Danaus & Ramesses/Seti = Aegyptus.

nodes.name: Dynasty XIX Horizon (Ramesside & Trojan War Synchronism)
sources: Budge Book of Kings Vol. II
nodes.notes: Manetho notes under Queen Twosret ('Thuoris') Troy was taken.

nodes.name: Dynasty XX Horizon (Ramesside II & Sea Peoples Defense)
nodes.era: 1189-1077 BCE (Budge Vol. II pp. 1-20; Manetho Fr. 57)
nodes.role: Ten Sons of Ramesses III to High Priest Herihor
sources: Budge Book of Kings Vol. II
nodes.notes: Concludes the New Kingdom down to Ramesses XI.

nodes.name: Dynasty XXI Horizon (Tanite Pharaohs & Theban Priest-Kings)
nodes.era: 1077-943 BCE (Budge Vol. II pp. 20-34; Manetho Fr. 58-59)
nodes.role: Divided Egypt (Biblical Era of David & Solomon)
sources: Budge Book of Kings Vol. II
nodes.notes: Siamun & Psusennes II in Tanis alongside High Priests Herihor to Pinudjem II at Thebes.

nodes.name: Dynasty XXII Horizon (Libyan Bubastite — Stele of Pasenhor)
nodes.era: 943-716 BCE (Budge Vol. II pp. 35-60; Manetho Fr. 60-61)
sources: Budge Book of Kings Vol. II
nodes.notes: Serapeum Stele of Pasenhor traces Shoshenq I back 6 generations to Buyuwawa and forward to Shoshenq V.

nodes.name: Dynasties XXIII–XXIV Horizon (Delta Coalitions & Bocchoris)
nodes.era: 818-715 BCE (Budge Vol. II pp. 60-69; Manetho Fr. 62-65)
sources: Budge Book of Kings Vol. II
nodes.notes: Pedubast I, Osorkon III, Tefnakht I & lawgiver Bakenranef (Bocchoris).

nodes.name: Dynasty XXV Horizon (Kushite Pharaohs & God's Wives Amenirdis/Shepenupet)
nodes.era: 744-656 BCE (Budge Vol. II pp. 70-78, 195-199; Manetho Fr. 66-67)
sources: Budge Book of Kings Vol. II
nodes.notes: Unifies Kushite royal family with 26th Dynasty Saite succession.

nodes.name: Dynasty XXVI Horizon (Saite Renaissance, 664–525 BCE)
nodes.era: 664-525 BCE (Budge Vol. II pp. 78-90; Manetho Fr. 68-69; Jer 44:30)
sources: Budge Book of Kings Vol. II
nodes.notes: Psamtik I, Necho II, Psamtik II, Apries (Hophra), Amasis II & Psamtik III.

nodes.name: Dynasties XXVII–XXXI Horizon (Persian Conquests & Last Native Pharaohs)
nodes.era: 525-332 BCE (Budge Vol. II pp. 91-106; Manetho Fr. 70-75)
nodes.role: Native Resistance Through Nectanebo II to Alexander (332 BCE)
sources: Budge Book of Kings Vol. II
nodes.notes: Amyrtaeus, Nepherites I, Hakor, Nectanebo I, Teos & Nectanebo II.

nodes.name: Ptolemaic Dynasty Horizon (Alexandria, 305–30 BCE)
nodes.role: Macedonian-Greek Pharaohs of Alexandria (Septuagint & Rosetta Stone)
sources: Budge Book of Kings Vol. II
nodes.notes: All 15 Ptolemies & 7 Cleopatras down to Cleopatra VII & Ptolemy XV Caesarion.

nodes.name: Napatan Kingdom of Kush Horizon (c. 653–315 BCE)
nodes.role: Post-25th Dynasty Nubian Pyramid Builders of Nuri
sources: Budge Book of the Kings of Egypt Vol. II (pp. 199-205)
nodes.notes: Napatan succession at Nuri & Jebel Barkal from Atlanersa through Nastasen.

nodes.name: Meroitic Kingdom Horizon (c. 270 BCE – 50 CE)
nodes.era: c. 270 BCE – 50 CE (Budge Vol. II pp. 205-214; Diodorus III.6; Acts 8:27)
sources: Budge Book of the Kings of Egypt Vol. II (pp. 205-214)
nodes.notes: Meroitic monarchs from Arqamani (Ergamenes) to Natakamani & Kandake Amanitore.

nodes.name: Djer / Kenkenes (Dyn. I, 47 yrs)
sources: Budge Book of Kings Vol. II
nodes.notes: Son of Hor-Aha; tomb at Abydos.

nodes.name: Djet / Uenephes (Dyn. I, 13 yrs)
sources: Budge Book of Kings Vol. II
nodes.notes: Son of Djer; wed Queen Merneith.

nodes.name: Queen Merneith (Regent of Dyn. I; Mother of Den)
sources: Budge Book of Kings Vol. II
nodes.notes: Consort of Djet and mother-regent for young King Den; buried with royal honors at Abydos.

nodes.name: Adjib / Miebis (Dyn. I)
sources: Budge Book of Kings Vol. II
nodes.notes: Son of Den.

nodes.name: Semerkhet / Semempses (Dyn. I)
sources: Budge Book of Kings Vol. II
nodes.notes: 7th king of the Thinite First Dynasty.

nodes.name: Qa'a / Bieneches (Dyn. I)
sources: Budge Book of Kings Vol. II
nodes.notes: Last king buried in the Abydos Umm el-Qa'ab royal necropolis.

nodes.name: Hotepsekhemwy / Boethos (Dyn. II Founder)
sources: Budge Book of Kings Vol. II
nodes.notes: Moved royal tombs to Saqqara.

nodes.name: Nebre / Kaiechos (Dyn. II)
sources: Budge Book of Kings Vol. II
nodes.notes: First pharaoh to incorporate Ra into his royal name.

nodes.name: Nynetjer / Binothris (Dyn. II)
sources: Budge Book of Kings Vol. II
nodes.notes: Manetho records that in his reign women were declared eligible to hold royal dignity.

nodes.name: Weneg / Tlas (Dyn. II)
sources: Budge Book of Kings Vol. II
nodes.notes: Mid-2nd Dynasty Memphite ruler.

nodes.name: Sened / Sethenes (Dyn. II)
sources: Budge Book of Kings Vol. II
nodes.notes: Revered in Memphite funerary cults.

nodes.name: Seth-Peribsen (Dyn. II)
sources: Budge Book of Kings Vol. II
nodes.notes: Took a Seth-name above his Abydos serekh before Khasekhemwy reconciled Horus and Seth.

nodes.name: Sanakht / Necherophes (Dyn. III)
sources: Budge Book of Kings Vol. II
nodes.notes: Elder brother/predecessor of Djoser; buried at Beit Khallaf.

nodes.name: Sekhemkhet / Tyris (Dyn. III)
sources: Budge Book of Kings Vol. II
nodes.notes: Builder of the Buried Pyramid at Saqqara.

nodes.name: Khaba (Dyn. III)
sources: Budge Book of Kings Vol. II
nodes.notes: Builder of the Layer Pyramid at Zawyet el-Aryan.

nodes.name: Huni / Kerpheres (Dyn. III)
sources: Budge Book of Kings Vol. II
nodes.notes: Father of Queen Hetepheres I and builder of Meidum.

nodes.name: Djedefre / Ratoises (Dyn. IV)
sources: Budge Book of Kings Vol. II
nodes.notes: Son of Khufu; built pyramid at Abu Rawash and first took 'Son of Ra' title.

nodes.name: Baka / Bicheris (Dyn. IV)
sources: Budge Book of Kings Vol. II
nodes.notes: Manetho's Bicheris placed amid Khufu's sons.

nodes.name: Shepseskaf (Dyn. IV)
sources: Budge Book of Kings Vol. II
nodes.notes: Built Mastabat el-Fir'aun at South Saqqara.

nodes.name: Queen Khentkawes I (Dyn. IV/V Bridge; 'Mother of Two Kings')
nodes.role: Daughter of Menkaure & Mother of Dyn. V
sources: Budge Book of Kings Vol. II
nodes.notes: Monument at Giza calls her 'King of Upper and Lower Egypt' and mother of Userkaf/Sahure.

nodes.name: Userkaf / Usercheres (Dyn. V Founder)
sources: Budge Book of Kings Vol. II
nodes.notes: Built the first solar temple at Abusir; Palermo Stone annals era.

nodes.name: Sahure / Sephres (Dyn. V)
sources: Budge Book of Kings Vol. II
nodes.notes: Dispatched first attested Egyptian maritime expedition to Punt.

nodes.name: Neferirkare Kakai (Dyn. V)
sources: Budge Book of Kings Vol. II
nodes.notes: Honored in the Abusir Papyri.

nodes.name: Shepseskare (Dyn. V)
sources: Budge Book of Kings Vol. II
nodes.notes: Brief Abusir ruler.

nodes.name: Neferefre (Dyn. V)
sources: Budge Book of Kings Vol. II
nodes.notes: Elder son of Neferirkare.

nodes.name: Nyuserre Ini (Dyn. V)
sources: Budge Book of Kings Vol. II
nodes.notes: Built solar temple at Abu Gorab.

nodes.name: Menkauhor (Dyn. V)
sources: Budge Book of Kings Vol. II
nodes.notes: Seventh king of Dynasty V.

nodes.name: Djedkare Isesi (Dyn. V)
sources: Budge Book of Kings Vol. II
nodes.notes: Era of Vizier Ptahhotep's Maxims.

nodes.name: Unas / Onnus (Last of Dyn. V — Pyramid Texts!)
sources: Budge Book of Kings Vol. II
nodes.notes: First ruler to carve the sacred Pyramid Texts inside his Saqqara tomb.

nodes.name: Teti / Othoes (Dyn. VI Founder)
sources: Budge Book of Kings Vol. II
nodes.notes: Married Princess Iput daughter of Unas.

nodes.name: Userkare (Dyn. VI)
sources: Budge Book of Kings Vol. II
nodes.notes: Brief ruler between Teti and Pepi I.

nodes.name: Pepi I / Phius (Dyn. VI)
sources: Budge Book of Kings Vol. II
nodes.notes: Expanded trade to Byblos & Nubia; father of Merenre I & Pepi II.

nodes.name: Merenre I (Dyn. VI)
sources: Budge Book of Kings Vol. II
nodes.notes: Received Nubian chiefs' homage at Elephantine.

nodes.name: Pepi II / Phiops (Dyn. VI — 94-Year Reign!)
sources: Budge Book of Kings Vol. II
nodes.notes: Ascended at age 6 and ruled into his 90s (Manetho: 94 yrs).

nodes.name: Merenre II Nemtyemsaf (Dyn. VI)
sources: Budge Book of Kings Vol. II
nodes.notes: Brief successor of aged Pepi II.

nodes.name: Queen Nitocris / Neith-iqerty (Close of Old Kingdom, Dyn. VI)
nodes.role: Last Sovereign of the Old Kingdom
sources: Budge Book of Kings Vol. II
nodes.notes: Described by Manetho as 'the noblest and loveliest of the women of her time' who built the third pyramid tradition.

nodes.name: Intef I (Theban Dyn. XI Founder)
sources: Budge Book of Kings Vol. II
nodes.notes: First Theban ruler to take a Horus name Sehertawy.

nodes.name: Intef II Wahankh (Dyn. XI)
sources: Budge Book of Kings Vol. II
nodes.notes: Pushed Theban power north to Abydos over 49-year reign.

nodes.name: Intef III (Dyn. XI)
sources: Budge Book of Kings Vol. II
nodes.notes: Father of unifier Mentuhotep II.

nodes.name: Mentuhotep III Sankhkare (Dyn. XI)
sources: Budge Book of Kings Vol. II
nodes.notes: Sent Hannu on Red Sea expedition to Punt.

nodes.name: Mentuhotep IV Nebtawyre (Last of Dyn. XI)
sources: Budge Book of Kings Vol. II
nodes.notes: Vizier Amenemhat (future Amenemhat I) led his Wadi Hammamat quarry expedition.

nodes.name: Amenemhat I (Dyn. XII Founder)
nodes.era: c. 1985–1955 BCE (Manetho Fr. 34; Breasted Vol. I)
sources: Budge Book of Kings Vol. II
nodes.notes: Founded Itjtawy; father of Senusret I.

nodes.name: Senusret I / Sesonchosis (Dyn. XII)
nodes.era: c. 1955–1911 BCE (Manetho Fr. 35; Story of Sinuhe)
sources: Budge Book of Kings Vol. II
nodes.notes: Built White Chapel at Karnak; era of Story of Sinuhe.

nodes.name: Amenemhat II (Dyn. XII)
sources: Budge Book of Kings Vol. II
nodes.notes: Expanded Near Eastern & Nubian trade.

nodes.name: Senusret II (Dyn. XII; Beni Hasan Era)
sources: Budge Book of Kings Vol. II
nodes.notes: Faiyum irrigation pioneer; Beni Hasan tomb painting of Semitic caravan of Abishai.

nodes.name: Amenemhat IV (Dyn. XII)
sources: Budge Book of Kings Vol. II
nodes.notes: Reigned 9 years before sister Sobekneferu.

nodes.name: Queen Sobekneferu / Scemiophris (First Attested Female Pharaoh, Dyn. XII)
sources: Budge Book of Kings Vol. II
nodes.notes: Sister of Amenemhat IV; Manetho explicitly notes Scemiophris 'reigned for 4 years' closing the 12th Dynasty.

nodes.name: Sobekhotep IV / Chenephres (Dyn. XIII; Artapanus's Moses Era)
sources: Budge Book of Kings Vol. II
nodes.notes: Identified in Waddell's Manetho notes with Artapanus's Pharaoh Chenephres.

nodes.name: Dedumose / Tutimaeus (Late Dyn. XIII; Manetho Hyksos Entry)
nodes.era: c. 1660 BCE (Manetho Fr. 42 via Josephus Ag. Ap. I.14)
nodes.role: Pharaoh Under Whom Hyksos Entered Egypt
sources: Budge Book of Kings Vol. II
nodes.notes: Named by Josephus quoting Manetho as Tutimaeus, when easterners seized Memphis without battle.

nodes.name: Salitis (1st Great Hyksos King of Avaris, Dyn. XV)
sources: Budge Book of Kings Vol. II
nodes.notes: Fortified Avaris in the Eastern Delta.

nodes.name: Khyan / Iannas (Great Hyksos King, Dyn. XV)
sources: Budge Book of Kings Vol. II
nodes.notes: Inscribed artifacts found from Knossos to Hattusa and Baghdad.

nodes.name: Apophis / Apepi (Hyksos King, Dyn. XV; Traditional Pharaoh of Joseph)
sources: Budge Book of Kings Vol. II
nodes.notes: Synchronized by George Syncellus as Pharaoh of Joseph; clashed with Seqenenre Tao.

nodes.name: Kamose (Last King of Dyn. XVII; Liberator Before Ahmose I)
sources: Budge Book of Kings Vol. II
nodes.notes: Drove Hyksos back to Avaris; succeeded by younger brother Ahmose I.

nodes.name: Amenhotep I (Son of Ahmose I; Deir el-Medina Founder, Dyn. XVIII)
sources: Budge Book of Kings Vol. II
nodes.notes: Consolidated Nubia and founded the royal artisans' village.

nodes.name: Thutmose II (Son of Thutmose I; Husband of Hatshepsut, Dyn. XVIII)
sources: Budge Book of Kings Vol. II
nodes.notes: Father of Thutmose III.

nodes.name: Queen Hatshepsut / Amessis (Regnant Female Pharaoh, Dyn. XVIII)
sources: Budge Book of Kings Vol. II
nodes.notes: Built Deir el-Bahari and dispatched fleet to Punt; co-regent with stepson Thutmose III.

nodes.name: Amenhotep II (Son of Thutmose III; Dyn. XVIII)
sources: Budge Book of Kings Vol. II
nodes.notes: Renowned archer-king who campaigned in Canaan.

nodes.name: Thutmose IV (Dream Stele Pharaoh; Father of Amenhotep III, Dyn. XVIII)
sources: Budge Book of Kings Vol. II
nodes.notes: Married Mitanni princess and restored Great Sphinx.

nodes.name: Queen Tiye (Wife of Amenhotep III; Mother of Akhenaten)
nodes.role: Great Royal Wife of Amenhotep III
sources: Budge Book of Kings Vol. II
nodes.notes: Daughter of Yuya & Tjuyu; mother of Akhenaten.

nodes.name: Queen Nefertiti (Great Royal Wife of Akhenaten)
nodes.role: Queen of Amarna & Mother-in-Law of Tutankhamun
sources: Budge Book of Kings Vol. II
nodes.notes: Bore six princesses incl. Ankhesenamun (wife of Tutankhamun).

nodes.name: Smenkhkare / Neferneferuaten (Amarna Co-Regent, Dyn. XVIII)
sources: Budge Book of Kings Vol. II
nodes.notes: Married Meritaten.

nodes.name: Pharaoh Ay (Successor of Tutankhamun, Dyn. XVIII)
sources: Budge Book of Kings Vol. II
nodes.notes: Former vizier & God's Father who buried Tutankhamun.

nodes.name: Horemheb / Harmais = Danaus (Manetho Fr. 50/53; Dyn. XVIII)
nodes.role: Final King of Dyn. XVIII Synchronized With Danaus
sources: Budge Book of Kings Vol. II
nodes.notes: Manetho explicitly equates Horemheb ('Harmais') fleeing Egypt to Argos with Greek King Danaus!

nodes.name: Ramesses I (Dyn. XIX Founder)
sources: Budge Book of Kings Vol. II
nodes.notes: Vizier Paramesse designated heir by Horemheb.

nodes.name: Seti I / Sethos (Father of Ramesses II; Manetho's Aegyptus!)
sources: Budge Book of Kings Vol. II
nodes.notes: Manetho equates Sethos with Aegyptus, brother of Harmais/Danaus; carved the Abydos King List.

nodes.name: Amenmesse (Dyn. XIX Rival)
sources: Budge Book of Kings Vol. II
nodes.notes: Reigned in Upper Egypt during Seti II's early years.

nodes.name: Seti II (Son of Merneptah; Dyn. XIX)
sources: Budge Book of Kings Vol. II
nodes.notes: Husband of Queen Twosret.

nodes.name: Siptah (Dyn. XIX)
sources: Budge Book of Kings Vol. II
nodes.notes: Ruled six years under stepmother Queen Twosret's regency.

nodes.name: Queen Twosret / Thuoris (Manetho's Trojan War Synchronism, Dyn. XIX)
sources: Budge Book of Kings Vol. II
nodes.notes: Manetho states Troy was taken during the reign of Thuoris (identified with Homer's Polybus/Alcandra).

nodes.name: Setnakhte (Dyn. XX Founder; Father of Ramesses III)
sources: Budge Book of Kings Vol. II
nodes.notes: Restored order and fathered Ramesses III.

nodes.name: Ramesses IV (Son of Ramesses III; Papyrus Harris I)
sources: Budge Book of Kings Vol. II
nodes.notes: Commissioned Great Harris Papyrus.

nodes.name: Ramesses V (Son of Ramesses IV)
sources: Budge Book of Kings Vol. II
nodes.notes: Turin Papyrus era.

nodes.name: Ramesses VI (Son of Ramesses III)
sources: Budge Book of Kings Vol. II
nodes.notes: Brother of Ramesses IV.

nodes.name: Ramesses VII (Son of Ramesses VI)
sources: Budge Book of Kings Vol. II
nodes.notes: Short Valley of the Kings reign.

nodes.name: Ramesses VIII (Son of Ramesses III)
nodes.role: Last Surviving Son of Ramesses III
sources: Budge Book of Kings Vol. II
nodes.notes: One-year reign.

nodes.name: Ramesses IX (Dyn. XX)
sources: Budge Book of Kings Vol. II
nodes.notes: 18-year reign.

nodes.name: Ramesses X (Dyn. XX)
sources: Budge Book of Kings Vol. II
nodes.notes: Predecessor of Ramesses XI.

nodes.name: Ramesses XI (Final Ramesside Pharaoh, Dyn. XX)
nodes.role: Last Pharaoh of Dynasty XX & New Kingdom
sources: Budge Book of Kings Vol. II
nodes.notes: Saw Rise of High Priest Herihor at Thebes & Smendes at Tanis (Report of Wenamun).

nodes.name: Herihor (High Priest of Amun & Ruler at Thebes)
sources: Budge Book of Kings Vol. II
nodes.notes: Assumed royal titles in Upper Egypt alongside Smendes in the Delta.

nodes.name: Piankh (High Priest of Amun)
sources: Budge Book of Kings Vol. II
nodes.notes: Father of Pinudjem I.

nodes.name: Pinudjem I (Theban Priest-King)
nodes.role: High Priest & Father of Psusennes I
sources: Budge Book of Kings Vol. II
nodes.notes: Wed Duathathor-Henuttawy (daughter of Ramesses XI!); father of Psusennes I & Menkheperre.

nodes.name: Menkheperre (High Priest of Amun)
sources: Budge Book of Kings Vol. II
nodes.notes: Fortified Upper Egypt; father of Pinudjem II.

nodes.name: Pinudjem II (High Priest of Amun; Royal Cache Founder)
sources: Budge Book of Kings Vol. II
nodes.notes: Fathered Psusennes II and preserved the New Kingdom royal mummies in DB320.

nodes.name: Smendes I (Dyn. XXI Founder at Tanis)
sources: Budge Book of Kings Vol. II
nodes.notes: Ruled Lower Egypt during Wenamun's mission to Byblos.

nodes.name: Psusennes I (Silver Pharaoh of Tanis, Dyn. XXI)
nodes.role: Son of Pinudjem I; King of Tanis
sources: Budge Book of Kings Vol. II
nodes.notes: Intact silver-coffin royal tomb excavated at Tanis.

nodes.name: Amenemope (Dyn. XXI; Contemporary of David)
sources: Budge Book of Kings Vol. II
nodes.notes: Ruled Tanis during David's monarchy.

nodes.name: Siamun (Dyn. XXI — Era of King Solomon & Gezer)
sources: Budge Book of Kings Vol. II
nodes.notes: Synchronized with early reign of King Solomon (cf. 1 Kgs 3:1, 9:16).

nodes.name: Psusennes II (Last of Dyn. XXI; Father-in-Law of Osorkon I)
sources: Budge Book of Kings Vol. II
nodes.notes: Son of Pinudjem II; daughter Maatkare married Osorkon I of Dyn. XXII.

nodes.name: Buyuwawa the Libyan (6-Gen Ancestor, Serapeum Stele of Pasenhor)
sources: Budge Book of Kings Vol. II
nodes.notes: Founder of the Meshwesh lineage recorded on the Serapeum Stele of Pasenhor.

nodes.name: Osorkon I (Son of Shoshenq I & Karamat; Dyn. XXII)
sources: Budge Book of Kings Vol. II
nodes.notes: Son of Shoshenq I; wed Maatkare (daughter of Psusennes II).

nodes.name: Takelot I (Son of Osorkon I, Dyn. XXII)
sources: Budge Book of Kings Vol. II
nodes.notes: Father of Osorkon II.

nodes.name: Osorkon II (Son of Takelot I, Dyn. XXII)
nodes.role: Ally of Ahab & Levant Coalition (853 BCE Battle of Qarqar Era)
sources: Budge Book of Kings Vol. II
nodes.notes: Sent Egyptian contingent noted with Ahab in Shalmaneser III's Kurkh Monolith.

nodes.name: Shoshenq II (Silver Falcon Coffin, Tanis, Dyn. XXII)
sources: Budge Book of Kings Vol. II
nodes.notes: Co-regent buried at Tanis.

nodes.name: Takelot II (Dyn. XXII)
sources: Budge Book of Kings Vol. II
nodes.notes: Chronicle of Prince Osorkon.

nodes.name: Shoshenq III (Dyn. XXII)
sources: Budge Book of Kings Vol. II
nodes.notes: 39-year reign at Tanis.

nodes.name: Pami (Dyn. XXII)
sources: Budge Book of Kings Vol. II
nodes.notes: Father of Shoshenq V.

nodes.name: Shoshenq V (Dyn. XXII; Pasenhor Stele Erected in Year 37!)
sources: Budge Book of Kings Vol. II
nodes.notes: Priestly Serapeum Stele of Pasenhor dated to his 37th regnal year.

nodes.name: Pedubast I (Dyn. XXIII Founder)
sources: Budge Book of Kings Vol. II
nodes.notes: Rival Theban-Leontopolitan king during Shoshenq III.

nodes.name: Osorkon III (Dyn. XXIII)
sources: Budge Book of Kings Vol. II
nodes.notes: Father of Takelot III & Shepenupet I.

nodes.name: Tefnakht I of Sais (Dyn. XXIV Founder vs. Piye)
nodes.era: 732–725 BCE (Budge Vol. II p.68; Victory Stele)
nodes.role: Chief of Sais & Dynasty XXIV Founder
sources: Budge Book of Kings Vol. II
nodes.notes: Fought Kushite King Piye (Piankhi Stele); father of Bocchoris.

nodes.name: Bakenranef / Bocchoris (Dyn. XXIV Lawgiver)
sources: Budge Book of Kings Vol. II
nodes.notes: Defeated by Kushite Shabaka when uniting Egypt under Dynasty XXV.

nodes.name: Shabaka / Sabacon (Dyn. XXV Pharaoh)
sources: Budge Book of Kings Vol. II
nodes.notes: Son of Kashta; defeated Bocchoris and unified all Egypt.

nodes.name: Shabataka / Sebichos (Dyn. XXV Pharaoh)
sources: Budge Book of Kings Vol. II
nodes.notes: Dispatched young Prince Taharqa northward to relieve Hezekiah.

nodes.name: Psamtik I (Dyn. XXVI Reunifier, 54-Year Reign!)
nodes.era: 664–610 BCE (Budge Vol. II p.79; Herodotus II)
sources: Budge Book of Kings Vol. II
nodes.notes: Son of Necho I of Sais; unified Egypt & expelled Assyrians; father of Necho II.

nodes.name: Psamtik II (Son of Necho II, Dyn. XXVI)
sources: Budge Book of Kings Vol. II
nodes.notes: Led 593 BCE Napatan expedition.

nodes.name: Apries / Biblical Pharaoh Hophra (Dyn. XXVI, Jer 44:30)
nodes.role: Son of Psamtik II; Sheltered Prophet Jeremiah
sources: Budge Book of Kings Vol. II
nodes.notes: Marched against Nebuchadnezzar II during 588 BCE siege of Jerusalem (Jer 37:5).

nodes.name: Amasis II / Ahmose II (Dyn. XXVI, 44-Year Reign!)
nodes.era: 570–526 BCE (Herodotus II.162; Budge Vol. II p.86)
sources: Budge Book of Kings Vol. II
nodes.notes: Promoted Greek Naucratis trade & allied with Croesus of Lydia.

nodes.name: Psamtik III (Last Native Saite King, 525 BCE)
nodes.role: Defeated at Pelusium by Cambyses II
sources: Budge Book of Kings Vol. II
nodes.notes: Fell to Persian conquest in 525 BCE.

nodes.name: Amyrtaeus of Sais (Sole King of Dyn. XXVIII, 404–399 BCE)
sources: Budge Book of Kings Vol. II
nodes.notes: Led native Egyptian revolt freeing Egypt from Darius II.

nodes.name: Nepherites I (Founder of Mendes Dyn. XXIX, 399–393 BCE)
sources: Budge Book of Kings Vol. II
nodes.notes: Allied with King Agesilaus II of Sparta against Persia.

nodes.name: Hakor / Achoris (Dyn. XXIX, 393–380 BCE)
sources: Budge Book of Kings Vol. II
nodes.notes: Repelled Persian invasion with Greek mercenaries.

nodes.name: Nectanebo I / Nakhtnebef (Founder of Dyn. XXX, 380–362 BCE)
sources: Budge Book of Kings Vol. II
nodes.notes: Fortified Delta & built Philae/Karnak pylons.

nodes.name: Teos / Tachos (Dyn. XXX, 362–360 BCE)
sources: Budge Book of Kings Vol. II
nodes.notes: Led joint Greco-Egyptian campaign into Phoenicia.

nodes.name: Nectanebo II / Nakhthorheb (LAST Native Pharaoh of Egypt, 360–343 BCE)
nodes.era: 360–343 BCE (Manetho Fr. 74; Budge Vol. II p.104)
sources: Budge Book of Kings Vol. II
nodes.notes: Nephew of Teos; deposed by Artaxerxes III in 343 BCE (Alexander Romance calls him Alexander's secret father!).

nodes.name: Ptolemy I Soter (+ Berenice I, 305–282 BCE)
sources: Budge Book of Kings Vol. II
nodes.notes: General of Alexander; built Alexandria & Library; father of Ptolemy II.

nodes.name: Ptolemy II Philadelphus (+ Arsinoe II; Sponsored Septuagint, 282–246 BCE)
nodes.era: 282–246 BCE (Budge Vol. II p.114; Letter of Aristeas)
nodes.role: Patron of Manetho & Septuagint Torah Translation
sources: Budge Book of Kings Vol. II
nodes.notes: Expanded Library of Alexandria and commissioned High Priest Eleazar's 72 translators.

nodes.name: Ptolemy III Euergetes (+ Berenice II, 246–222 BCE)
sources: Budge Book of Kings Vol. II
nodes.notes: Canopus Decree.

nodes.name: Ptolemy IV Philopator (+ Arsinoe III, 222–204 BCE)
sources: Budge Book of Kings Vol. II
nodes.notes: Victor of Raphia (217 BCE) over Antiochus III.

nodes.name: Ptolemy V Epiphanes (+ Cleopatra I Syra; Rosetta Stone, 204–180 BCE)
nodes.era: 204–180 BCE (Budge Vol. II p.126; Memphis Decree)
sources: Budge Book of Kings Vol. II
nodes.notes: Issued the trilingual Rosetta Stone (196 BCE) and wed Seleucid Princess Cleopatra I Syra.

nodes.name: Ptolemy VI Philometor (+ Cleopatra II; Patron of Onias IV, 180–145 BCE)
nodes.era: 180–145 BCE (Budge Vol. II p.129; Josephus Ant. XIII.3)
nodes.role: Elder Son of Ptolemy V & Cleopatra I Syra
sources: Budge Book of Kings Vol. II
nodes.notes: Granted Leontopolis to Jewish High Priest Onias IV.

nodes.name: Ptolemy VIII Euergetes II Physcon (+ Cleopatra III, 170–116 BCE)
sources: Budge Book of Kings Vol. II
nodes.notes: Grandfather of Cleopatra VII.

nodes.name: Ptolemy IX Soter II Lathyros (116–81 BCE)
nodes.role: Son of Ptolemy VIII & Cleopatra III
sources: Budge Book of Kings Vol. II
nodes.notes: Father of Ptolemy XII Auletes.

nodes.name: Ptolemy X Alexander I (+ Berenice III, 107–88 BCE)
sources: Budge Book of Kings Vol. II
nodes.notes: Co-regent & uncle of Ptolemy XII.

nodes.name: Ptolemy XII Auletes (Father of Cleopatra VII, 80–51 BCE)
sources: Budge Book of Kings Vol. II
nodes.notes: Father of Cleopatra VII, Berenice IV, Arsinoe IV, Ptolemy XIII & Ptolemy XIV.

nodes.name: Ptolemy XV Caesarion (Son of Cleopatra VII & Julius Caesar, d. 30 BCE)
sources: Budge Book of Kings Vol. II
nodes.notes: Eldest son of Cleopatra VII by Julius Caesar; slain after Actium.

nodes.name: Ptolemy XIII Theos Philopator (Son of Ptolemy XII, d. 47 BCE)
nodes.notes: Drowned in the Nile during the Alexandrian War.

nodes.name: Ptolemy XIV (Younger Brother of Cleopatra VII, d. 44 BCE)
nodes.notes: Nominal co-ruler alongside Cleopatra VII.

nodes.name: Atlanersa of Napata (Son of Taharqa / Tantamani Era)
sources: Budge Book of the Kings of Egypt Vol. II (pp.195–214)
nodes.notes: Buried at Nuri.

nodes.name: Senkamanisken of Napata
sources: Budge Book of the Kings of Egypt Vol. II (pp.195–214)
nodes.notes: Father of Anlamani & Aspelta.

nodes.name: Anlamani of Napata
sources: Budge Book of the Kings of Egypt Vol. II (pp.195–214)
nodes.notes: Crowned at Kawa; elder brother of Aspelta.

nodes.name: Aspelta (Moved Kushite Capital South to Meroe, c. 593 BCE)
sources: Budge Book of the Kings of Egypt Vol. II (pp.195–214)
nodes.notes: Resisted Psamtik II's 593 BCE expedition and transferred center to Meroe.

nodes.name: Harsiotef of Kush
sources: Budge Book of the Kings of Egypt Vol. II (pp.195–214)
nodes.notes: Stele of 35 regnal years.

nodes.name: Nastasen of Kush (Last Great Napatan Tomb at Nuri)
sources: Budge Book of the Kings of Egypt Vol. II (pp.195–214)
nodes.notes: Defended Nubia against Khababash era forces.

nodes.name: Arqamani / King Ergamenes of Meroe (Friend of Ptolemy II & IV)
nodes.era: c. 270–220 BCE (Diodorus III.6; Budge Vol. II)
sources: Budge Book of the Kings of Egypt Vol. II (pp.195–214)
nodes.notes: Greek-educated Meroitic king mentioned by Diodorus Siculus.

nodes.name: King Natakamani of Meroe (Husband of Kandake Amanitore)
sources: Budge Book of the Kings of Egypt Vol. II (pp.195–214)
nodes.notes: Co-ruler with Kandake Queen Amanitore during Meroe's architectural zenith.

nodes.name: Queen Amanitore (Kandake / Biblical 'Candace' Era)
nodes.era: c. 1–20 CE (Budge Vol. II p.214; Acts 8:27)
sources: Budge Book of the Kings of Egypt Vol. II (pp.195–214)
nodes.notes: Built Lion Temple at Naqa & restored Amun temple at Meroe; maternal figure of Acts 8:27 'Candace' dynasty.

nodes.name: Crown Prince Arikhankharer (Son of Natakamani & Amanitore)
sources: Budge Book of the Kings of Egypt Vol. II (pp.195–214)
nodes.notes: Depicted with Natakamani & Amanitore at Naqa.

nodes.name: King Shorkaror (Son of Natakamani & Amanitore)
sources: Budge Book of the Kings of Egypt Vol. II (pp.195–214)
nodes.notes: Inscribed victory relief at Jebel Qeili.
